'''Chen Bang-yen''' ([[traditional Chinese]]: 陳邦彦; born October 3, 1943) is a Taiwanese-American [[mathematician]] who works mainly on [[differential geometry]] and related subjects. He was a University Distinguished Professor of [[Michigan State University]] from 1990 to 2012 until his retirement. After 2012, he became University Distinguished [[Professor Emeritus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.msu.edu/News/2024/bang-yen-chen.aspx |title=MSU Math Department News}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Chen was born in [[Toucheng]], Taiwan. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] from [[Tamkang University]] in 1965 and his [[Master of Science|M.S.]] from [[National Tsing Hua University]] in 1967.  He obtained his [[Ph.D.]] degree from the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 1970 under the supervision of [[Tadashi Nagano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onesearch.library.nd.edu/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=ndu_aleph000312527&context=L&vid=NDU&lang=en_US&search_scope=malc_blended&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=onesearch&query=any,contains,Chen,%20Bang-yen&sortby=rank&facet=rtype,include,dissertations&offset=0|title=Chen Bang-yen's Ph.D. thesis}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=15594 |title=Chen Bang-yen on Genealogy Project
}}</ref>

== Career ==
Chen Bang-yen taught at Tamkang University between 1965 and 1968 and at  National Tsing Hua University during the academic year 1967–1968. After completing his doctoral studies (1968-1970) at the University of Notre  Dame, he joined the faculty at Michigan State University as a research associate from 1970 to 1972. He became an associate professor in 1972 and a full professor in 1976. He was awarded the title of University Distinguished Professor in 1990. After 2012, he became University Distinguished Professor Emeritus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.msu.edu/directory/PersonalPage.aspx?id=111111244 |title=Chen Bang-yen on MSU domain}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ze7siAcAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Chen Bang-yen on Google Scholar}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/3846342|title=Bang-Yen Chen: His Life and Works}}</ref>

Chen Bang-yen is the author of over 600 works, including 12 books, spanning more than six decades. His works have been cited over 40,000 times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Bang_Yen_Chen |title=Chen Bang-yen on ResearchGate}}</ref>
He also co-edited five books,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=chen%2C+Bang-yen |title=Chen Bang-yen on Zentralblatt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Bang_Yen_Chen|title= Chen Bang-yen on Research Gate}}</ref> four of which were published by Springer<ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-16-0021-0 |title=Complex geometry of slant submanifolds|date=2022 |doi=10.1007/978-981-16-0021-0 |isbn=978-981-16-0020-3 |editor-last1=Chen |editor-last2=Shahid |editor-last3=Al-Solamy |editor-first1=Bang-Yen |editor-first2=Mohammad Hasan |editor-first3=Falleh }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-16-0017-3 |title=Contact geometry of slant submanifolds|date=2022 |doi=10.1007/978-981-16-0017-3 |isbn=978-981-16-0016-6 |editor-last1=Chen |editor-last2=Shahid |editor-last3=Al-Solamy |editor-first1=Bang-Yen |editor-first2=Mohammad Hasan |editor-first3=Falleh }}</ref>
<ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-99-9750-3 |title=Geometry of submanifolds and application|series=Infosys Science Foundation Series |date=2024 |doi=10.1007/978-981-99-9750-3 |isbn=978-981-99-9749-7 }}
</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/9789819551477 |title=Geometric inequalities and applications|date=2026 |isbn=978-981-95-5147-7 |editor-last1=Chen |editor-last2=Choudhary  |editor-first1=Bang-Yen |editor-first2=Majid Ali }}</ref> and one of which by the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.ams.org/books/conm/777/ |title=Differential geometry and global analysis|series=Contemporary Mathematics |date=2022 |volume=777 |doi=10.1090/conm/777 |isbn=978-1-4704-6874-3 }}</ref>

In 1989, Chen Bang-yen became an elected corresponding member of Accademia Peloritana dei Pericolanti, Italy. In 2008, Chen was presented with the first Geometry Prize from the Simon Stevin Institute for Geometry, Netherlands, for his seminal contributions to differential geometry.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://webbut.unitbv.ro/index.php/Series_III/article/view/2188 |title=Simon Stevin prize for geometry |journal=Bulletin of the Transilvania University of Brasov. Series III: Mathematics and Computer Science |date=30 November 2008 |pages=161–164 |last1=Gielis |first1=Johan }}</ref>
He was named as one of the top 15 famous Taiwanese scientists by the SCI Journal in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scijournal.org/articles/famous-taiwanese-scientists |title=Top 15 Famous Taiwanese Scientists|date=26 September 2022 }}</ref> Chen Bang-yen was awarded doctorates from the Science University of Tokyo (D.Sc. 1981) and Ovidius University of Constanța (Dr.h.c. 2025).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cugetliber.ro/stiri-cultura-educatie-universitatea-ovidius-acorda-titlul-de-doctor-honoris-causa-unei-personalitati-a-geometriei-mondiale-529974#google_vignette |title=Doctor Honoris Causa |date=26 May 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ordinea.ro/universitatea-ovidius-acorda-titlul-de-doctor-honoris-causa-prof-univ-dr-bang-yen-chen |title=Doctor Honoris Causa II |date=26 May 2025 }}</ref>
On October 20–21, 2018, at the 1143rd Meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]] held at [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], one of the Special Sessions was dedicated to Chen's 75th birthday.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/meetings/sectional/2259_special.html|title=American Mathematical Society, Meeting No. 1143}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201805/201805FullIssue.pdf |title=Notices of AMS}}</ref> The volume 756 in the Contemporary Mathematics series, published by the American Mathematical Society, is dedicated to Chen Bang-yen, and it includes many contributions presented in the Ann Arbor event.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.ams.org/books/conm/756/|title=Contemporary Mathematics, Volume 756|year=2020 |volume=756 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |doi=10.1090/conm/756 |isbn=9781470450922 |s2cid=230645373 }}</ref> The volume is edited by Joeri Van der Veken, Alfonso Carriazo, Ivko Dimitrić, Yun Myung Oh, [[Bogdan Suceavă]], and Luc Vrancken. On July 15–16, 2024, the 9th European Congress of Mathematics held at Seville, Spain, includes in its program a mini symposium on Geometry of Submanifolds, celebrating Chen Bang-yen's 80th Anniversary.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.ecm2024sevilla.com/index.php/program/ecm2024-programme-mini-symposia |title=MS8-Min-symposium at 9th European Congress of Mathematics}}</ref>

==Research contributions==
In [[symmetric spaces]], Chen Bang-yen and [[Tadashi Nagano]] created the (M+,M-)-theory (also known as the Chen-Nagano theory) for compact symmetric spaces with important applications to several areas in mathematics.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-belgian-mathematical-society-simon-stevin/volume-25/issue-4/Two-numbers-and-their-applications---A-survey/10.36045/bbms/1546570911.ful |title=Two-numbers and applications|journal=Bulletin of the Belgian Mathematical Society - Simon Stevin |date=December 2018 |volume=25 |issue=4 |pages=565–596 |doi=10.36045/bbms/1546570911 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |arxiv=1805.04796 }}</ref>
<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.ams.org/books/conm/777/ |title=(M+,M-)-theory|series=Contemporary Mathematics |date=2022 |volume=777 |doi=10.1090/conm/777 |isbn=978-1-4704-6874-3 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://rjm-cs.utcb.ro/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/2024v14i1_6.pdf#page=1 |title=Designs in Compact Symmetric Spaces}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/3736056 |title=Furuki and Tamaru's paper}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://doi.org/10.1142/9789814566285_0018 |title=Tanaka's paper|doi=10.1142/9789814566285_0018 }}</ref> One of the advantages of their theory is that it is powerful for applying inductive arguments on polars or meridians.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rjm-cs.utcb.ro/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/2023v13i2_2.pdf#page=1 |title=Romanian Journal of Mathematics and computer Science}}</ref> In particularly, Chen and Nagano initiated the study of maximal antipodal set and 2-number (also known as Chen-Nagano invariant);<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1988-308-01/S0002-9947-1988-0946443-8/ |title=2-number|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |date=1988 |volume=308 |issue=1 |pages=273–297 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1988-0946443-8 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |last2=Nagano |first2=Tadashi |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1993-118-04/S0002-9939-1993-1163336-1/ |title=Chen-Nagano invariant|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |date=1993 |volume=118 |issue=4 |pages=1237–1242 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1993-1163336-1 |last1=Sánchez |first1=Cristián U. }}</ref>
as an application Chen and Nagano were able to completely determine 2-rank of all compact simple [[Lie groups]] and thus they settled a problem in [[group theory]] raised by prominent mathematicians [[Armand Borel]] and [[Jean-Pierre Serre]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02564557 |title=Borel and Serre's paper paper |doi=10.1007/BF02564557 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1988-308-01/S0002-9947-1988-0946443-8/ |title=Application to Borel-Serre problem|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |date=1988 |volume=308 |issue=1 |pages=273–297 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1988-0946443-8 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |last2=Nagano |first2=Tadashi |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1993, Chen Bang-yen studied submanifolds of [[space form]]s, showing that the intrinsic [[sectional curvature]] at any point is bounded below in terms of the intrinsic [[scalar curvature]], the length of the [[mean curvature]] vector, and the curvature of the space form. Consequently, given a minimal submanifold of Euclidean space, every sectional curvature at a point is greater than or equal to one-half of the scalar curvature at that point. Interestingly, the submanifolds for which the inequality is an equality can be characterized as certain products of minimal surfaces of low dimension with Euclidean spaces.

In [[Riemannian geometry]], Chen Bang-yen invented the theory of ''δ-invariants'' (also known as ''Chen invariants''), which are certain kinds of partial [[Trace (linear algebra)|traces]] of the [[sectional curvature]];<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/math1924/26/1/26_1_105/_article/ |title=New type of Riemannian invariants|journal=Japanese Journal of Mathematics |series=New Series |date=2000 |volume=26 |issue=1 |pages=105–127 |doi=10.4099/math1924.26.105 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |doi-access=free }}</ref> they can be viewed as an interpolation between sectional curvature and [[scalar curvature]], allowing for more nuanced analysis of submanifolds.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/8003#t=aboutBook/ |title=δ-Invariants and Applications|date=2011 |doi=10.1142/8003 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |isbn=978-981-4329-63-7 }}</ref> Due to the Gauss equation, the δ-invariants of a Riemannian [[submanifold]] can be controlled by the length of the [[mean curvature|mean curvature vector]] and the size of the sectional curvature of the ambient manifold. Submanifolds of [[space forms]] that satisfy the equality case of this inequality are known as ''ideal immersions''; such submanifolds are critical points of a certain restriction of the [[Willmore energy]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/8003#t=aboutBook/ |title=Pseudo-Riemannian geometry, δ-Invariants and Applications|date=2011 |doi=10.1142/8003 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |isbn=978-981-4329-63-7 }}</ref> Also in [[Riemannian geometry]], Chen Bang-yen and [[Kentaro Yano (mathematician)|Kentaro Yano]] initiated the study of spaces of quasi-constant curvature.

In [[differential geometry]], Chen Bang-yen also created the theory of finite type submanifolds,<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/9237#t=aboutBook|title=Submanifolds of finite type|series=Series in Pure Mathematics |date=2014 |volume=27 |doi=10.1142/9237 |isbn=978-981-4616-68-3 }}</ref> which studies submanifolds of a Euclidean space for which the position vector is a finite linear combination of eigenfunctions of the [[Laplace-Beltrami operator]]. As a by-product, Chen proposed his longstanding biharmonic conjecture in 1991, stating that any biharmonic submanifold in a Euclidean space must be a [[minimal submanifold]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/9237#t=aboutBook |title=Book on submanifolds of finite type, 2nd edition|series=Series in Pure Mathematics |date=2014 |volume=27 |doi=10.1142/9237 |isbn=978-981-4616-68-3 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0001870821001353 |title=Fu's paper on biharmonic conjecture|doi=10.1016/j.aim.2021.107697 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/11610#t=aboutBook |title=Book on biharmonic submanifolds and maps|date=2020 |doi=10.1142/11610 |last1=Ou |first1=Ye-Lin |last2=Chen |first2=Bang-Yen |isbn=978-981-12-1237-6 }}</ref>

In [[complex geometry]], Chen Bang-yen created the theory of slant submanifolds.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Slant immersions |date=1990 |doi=10.1017/S0004972700017925 |last1=Chen |first1=Bang-Yen |journal=Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society |volume=41 |pages=135–147 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-16-0021-0 |title=Complex geometry of slant submanifolds|date=2022 |doi=10.1007/978-981-16-0021-0 |isbn=978-981-16-0020-3 |editor-last1=Chen |editor-last2=Shahid |editor-last3=Al-Solamy |editor-first1=Bang-Yen |editor-first2=Mohammad Hasan |editor-first3=Falleh }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-16-0017-3 |title=Contact geometry of slant submanifolds|date=2022 |doi=10.1007/978-981-16-0017-3 |isbn=978-981-16-0016-6 |editor-last1=Chen |editor-last2=Shahid |editor-last3=Al-Solamy |editor-first1=Bang-Yen |editor-first2=Mohammad Hasan |editor-first3=Falleh }}</ref>
A ''slant submanifold'' of an almost Hermitian manifold is a submanifold for which there is a number {{mvar|θ}} such that the image under the almost complex structure of an arbitrary submanifold tangent vector has an angle of {{mvar|θ}} with the submanifold's tangent space.
Within the context of [[almost Hermitian manifold]]s, Chen also initiated the theory of the geometry of warped product submanifolds by establishing sharp relationships between the warping function and mean curvature of warped product submanifolds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/proceedings-of-the-edinburgh-mathematical-society/article/on-isometric-minimal-immersions-from-warped-products-into-real-space-forms/6F61641F51B02B776AA384FCC6548BFB |title= Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society |doi= 10.1017/S001309150100075X}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/rocky-mountain-journal-of-mathematics/volume-34/issue-2/Warped-Products-in-Real-Space-Forms/10.1216/rmjm/1181069867.full |title= Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics|doi= 10.1007/s10714-014-1833-9|arxiv= 1411.0270}}</ref> In particular, he introduced the study of CR-[[warped product]] [[submanifold]]s,  providing a new method to investigate CR-submanifolds and their extensions by utilizing the concept of [[warped product]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s006050170019 |title= CR-warped products I|doi= 10.1007/s006050170019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s006050170002 |title= CR-warped product II |doi=10.1007/s006050170002}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00605-002-0009-y |title= CR-warped products with compact holomorphic factor|doi= 10.1007/s00605-002-0009-y}}</ref>

In [[general relativity]] and [[gravitational]] [[theory]], Chen Bang-yen established a simple and useful characterization of generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes; namely, a [[Lorentzian manifold]] is a generalized Robertson-Walker spacetime [[if and only if]] it admits a timelike concircular vector field.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10714-014-1833-9 |title= General Relativity and Gravitation|doi= 10.1007/s10714-014-1833-9|arxiv= 1411.0270|last1= Chen|first1= Bang-Yen|date= 2014}}</ref>

Given an [[almost Hermitian manifold]], a totally real submanifold is one for which the tangent space is orthogonal to its image under the almost complex structure. From the algebraic structure of the [[Gauss-Codazzi equations|Gauss equation]] and the Simons formula, Chen Bang-yen and Koichi Ogiue derived several information on submanifolds of complex space forms which are totally real and [[minimal surface|minimal]]. By using [[Shiing-Shen Chern]], [[Manfredo do Carmo]], and [[Shoshichi Kobayashi]]'s estimate<ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-25588-5_5 |title=Minimal submanifolds of a sphere|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-25588-5_5 }}</ref> of the algebraic terms in the [[Simons' formula|Simons formula]], Chen and Ogiue showed that closed submanifolds which are totally real and minimal must be totally geodesic if the second fundamental form is sufficiently small. By using the Codazzi equation and [[isothermal coordinates]], they also obtained rigidity results on two-dimensional closed submanifolds of complex space forms, which are totally real.
